Command: Hide at Cherith, Go to Zarephath
Summary: God's drought-exile commands to Elijah: hide by the brook Cherith, then go to Zarephath and dwell there.
Commandment: Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith; then arise, get thee to Zarephath, and dwell there.
Application: Merged row: two moves under one itinerant commission — hide by Cherith (1 Kings 17:3, ravens fed him) then go to Zarephath (17:9, the widow sustained him). Parent may split into two rows; kept merged because both are stages of the same drought exile, not two missions.
Purpose: To hide and sustain Elijah through the drought God had announced — by ravens at Cherith, by a widow at Zarephath (1 Kings 17:4-6, 17:9).
Function: Two moves under one itinerant commission — hide by Cherith, then go to Zarephath. This was a one-time command, given once for a specific drought, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not apply to it. Its goal was to hide and sustain Elijah through the drought God had announced — by ravens at Cherith, by a widow at Zarephath. The evil or restraint angle does not apply here; this was provision for one prophet in one famine, not a law against a recurring evil. He was fed by ravens, then sustained by the widow.
